correctness.rationale: Independently generated all six-edge subsets with twelve distinct endpoints and all their faces: 20 matchings and face counts (18,117,276,270,120,20). Using exact integers and a different reduction order, I first split off the image of the signed degree-three boundary using 170 unit pivots (zero residual), then computed the kernel of the induced degree-two boundary on the 106 free quotient coordinates using 100 unit pivots (zero residual). The projection and section checks and zero boundary composition leave an integral H2 basis of rank six, not just a rational rank. The one-column rotation, including reordering signs, acts in this independent basis with order six, characteristic polynomial x^6−1, and Smith diagonal (1,1,1,1,3,0) for R−I. This verifies the regular rational character and coinvariants Z ⊕ Z/3. In the frozen displayed basis, column relations 1 and 3 give e4=e6 and e1+e3=−e6; columns 6 and 5 give e2=−2e6 and e5=−e6; column 2 gives 3e6=0 and column 4 duplicates e4=e6. The asserted obstruction to an integral regular lattice follows.
residual_risks: The calculation is for this exact 18-edge graph and one rotation only; it gives neither full dihedral-module structure nor quotient-space homology.
